text:
maria: Starting a PRD draft for Scoped Credentials (org/projects + API keys + scoped tokens). Need acceptance criteria, edge cases, and launch SLOs. Quick sync pls.

deepak: +1. I'll add runtime requirements (auth lookup latency, cache TTLs).

kate: Customer ask: project-scoped API keys that only access embeddings endpoints. Also need deny-lists (explicit denies).

sylvie: UX question — how do we surface token scopes in the console? Human-readable labels + raw JSON policy for audit. Also need copy-to-clip for keys.

aj: Migration concern: existing API keys are full-access. We need a clear path: tag legacy keys, opt-in scoping, and automatic expiry window.

maria: Draft acceptance criteria: 
- Tokens can be constrained by org -> project -> route (model/endpoint).
- Tokens support expiration and rotation (client and server flows).
- Admins can revoke at org or project scope and revoke is enforced globally within 30s.
- Audit logs for every token creation, usage, and revoke.
- Console shows token policy and last-used timestamp.

deepak: Edge cases to capture:
- Overlapping allow/deny rules across org/project: need deterministic precedence.
- Token used across Dedicated/Private where control plane access may be intermittent — define fallback behavior.
- SDKs that batch requests for multiple projects: ensure token+project pairing preserved.
- Rate-limited audit exports for high-volume customers.

sylvie: Policy templates idea: `read-only-embeddings`, `inference-no-training`, `limited-rate-10rps`. Will mock presets in console.

kate: Proposed launch criteria:
- Feature-flagged rollout in prod.
- 10 customers in beta, at least 1 enterprise with legal/compliance sign-off.
- Perf: auth lookup median < 2ms, P95 < 15ms.
- Observability: per-token traces + rate-limited audit export available to customers.

aj: Tradeoffs: Edge caching improves latency but increases window where revoked tokens may still work. Default cache TTL 30s; ops can tighten. Documented in PRD.

deepak: Implementation sketch:
1) Token service + policy engine (evaluate allow/deny, precedence).
2) Strong cache layer (LRU + TTL) at edge and mid-tier.
3) Audit writer that batches events to event-store.
Security note: store only hashed token IDs, not raw tokens.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary deploy scheduled: `auth-service:v2` -> 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC.

maria: Next steps: deepak to fold acceptance criteria into PRD; sylvie to add console mockups; aj to draft migration plan + rollback. Reconvene Friday 10am PT.

sylvie: I'll upload mocks by Thu EOD to the PRD doc (Figma link will be in doc).

kate: I'll draft the customer beta checklist and ping legal for compliance items.

aj: Migration plan (high level): script tags existing keys as `legacy`; opt-in scoping endpoint; 2-week opt-in window; telemetry to detect breakage; rollback script ready.

deepak: Precedence rule proposal: explicit `deny` always overrides `allow`. Project-level `allow` can be allowed to override org-level `deny` only if `allow_project_override=true` in org policy (explicit opt-in). I'll add examples to PRD.

maria: Great work team. Adding all of this to the PRD now and will open RFC PR for review. cc @here if anyone wants to weigh in on acceptance criteria or edge cases.

sylvie: small UI question — do we show token scopes in audit exports? If yes, we need column mapping.

kate: yes, include `token_id`, `scope_label`, `project_id`, `actor`, `timestamp`. Keep export sizes capped.

aj: Also note: migration telemetry should flag SDK versions that don't send `project_id` in headers. We'll require a 2-week minimum runway.

maria: Perfect — tracking action items in PRD with owners. Thanks.
